items.title: 不甜的布丁
items.title_de: Der Pudding, der nicht süß ist
items.title_pt: O pudim que não é doce
items.dek: 一顿英国的星期天午饭，一个让小月很意外的“布丁”。
paragraphs: 小月在英国曼彻斯特读书。上个星期六，她的同学Emily问她：“明天中午你有空吗？来我家吃Sunday roast吧！”小月不知道这是什么，可是她很高兴地说：“好啊！”
Emily告诉她，Sunday roast就是“星期天的烤肉”。很多英国家庭星期天会一起吃这顿饭，有烤牛肉或者烤鸡，还有土豆、胡萝卜和别的蔬菜。“对了，还有约克郡布丁，”Emily说，“我奶奶做的最好吃。”
小月听了很开心。她最喜欢吃布丁了，以为饭后会有一个甜甜的小点心。
星期天，Emily的奶奶把一盘热热的东西放在桌子上。它们黄黄的，中间是空的，样子像一个小碗。小月尝了一口——一点儿也不甜！奶奶笑着说：“这就是约克郡布丁，是用鸡蛋、面粉和牛奶做的。要和肉一起吃，上面再放一点儿肉汁。”
小月又吃了两个，觉得比她想的还好吃。吃完饭，她说：“下次我请你们吃饺子吧！我做的饺子没有奶奶的布丁好看，但是也很好吃。”大家都笑了。
paragraphs_en: Xiaoyue is studying in Manchester, England. Last Saturday her classmate Emily asked her: “Are you free tomorrow at lunchtime? Come to my place for a Sunday roast!” Xiaoyue didn't know what that was, but she happily said: “Sure!”

Emily told her that a Sunday roast is “the roast on Sunday”. Many British families eat this meal together on Sundays: roast beef or roast chicken, with potatoes, carrots and other vegetables. “Oh, and there are Yorkshire puddings,” Emily said. “My grandma makes the best ones.”
Xiaoyue was very pleased to hear that. She loves pudding more than anything, and thought there would be a sweet little treat after the meal.

On Sunday, Emily's grandma put a plate of something hot on the table. They were golden yellow and hollow in the middle, shaped like little bowls. Xiaoyue took a bite — not sweet at all! Grandma said with a smile: “This is Yorkshire pudding. It's made from eggs, flour and milk. You eat it with the meat and pour a little gravy on top.”

Xiaoyue ate two more and thought they were even tastier than she had imagined. After the meal she said: “Next time I'll treat you to dumplings! My dumplings don't look as nice as Grandma's puddings, but they taste very good too.” Everyone laughed.
paragraphs_de: Xiaoyue studiert in Manchester in England. Letzten Samstag fragte ihre Kommilitonin Emily sie: „Hast du morgen Mittag Zeit? Komm zu uns zum Sunday Roast!“ Xiaoyue wusste nicht, was das ist, aber sie sagte fröhlich: „Gern!“

Emily erklärte ihr, dass Sunday Roast „der Sonntagsbraten“ ist. Viele britische Familien essen diese Mahlzeit sonntags zusammen: Roastbeef oder Brathähnchen, dazu Kartoffeln, Karotten und anderes Gemüse. „Ach ja, und es gibt Yorkshire Puddings“, sagte Emily. „Meine Oma macht die besten.“
Xiaoyue freute sich sehr, als sie das hörte. Pudding mag sie am allerliebsten, und sie dachte, nach dem Essen gäbe es eine kleine süße Nachspeise.

Am Sonntag stellte Emilys Oma einen Teller mit etwas Heißem auf den Tisch. Die Dinger waren goldgelb, in der Mitte hohl und sahen aus wie kleine Schüsseln. Xiaoyue probierte einen Bissen – überhaupt nicht süß! Die Oma sagte lächelnd: „Das ist Yorkshire Pudding. Er wird aus Eiern, Mehl und Milch gemacht. Man isst ihn zum Fleisch und gibt oben ein bisschen Bratensoße darauf.“

Xiaoyue aß noch zwei und fand sie noch leckerer, als sie gedacht hatte. Nach dem Essen sagte sie: „Nächstes Mal lade ich euch zu Jiaozi ein! Meine Teigtaschen sehen nicht so schön aus wie Omas Puddings, aber sie schmecken auch sehr gut.“ Alle lachten.
paragraphs_pt: Xiaoyue estuda em Manchester, na Inglaterra. No sábado passado, a colega dela, Emily, perguntou: “Você está livre amanhã na hora do almoço? Vem almoçar um Sunday roast lá em casa!” Xiaoyue não sabia o que era isso, mas respondeu toda contente: “Claro!”

Emily explicou que Sunday roast é “o assado de domingo”. Muitas famílias britânicas comem essa refeição juntas aos domingos: rosbife ou frango assado, com batatas, cenouras e outros legumes. “Ah, e tem Yorkshire pudding”, disse Emily. “O da minha avó é o melhor.”
Xiaoyue ficou muito feliz ao ouvir isso. Ela adora pudim e achou que depois da comida teria um docinho.

No domingo, a avó da Emily colocou na mesa um prato com uma coisa quentinha. Eram douradinhos, ocos no meio e tinham a forma de tigelinhas. Xiaoyue deu uma mordida — não era nada doce! A avó disse sorrindo: “Isto é Yorkshire pudding. É feito com ovos, farinha e leite. Come-se com a carne, com um pouco de molho por cima.”

Xiaoyue comeu mais dois e achou ainda mais gostoso do que tinha imaginado. Depois do almoço, ela disse: “Da próxima vez eu convido vocês para comer jiaozi! Os meus jiaozi não são tão bonitos quanto os puddings da vovó, mas também são muito gostosos.” Todo mundo riu.
items.grammar: A 没有 B + adjective means 'A is not as … as B': 我做的饺子没有奶奶的布丁好看 'my dumplings don't look as nice as Grandma's puddings'. Compare A 比 B 还 + adjective, 'A is even more … than B': 比她想的还好吃 'even tastier than she imagined'.
items.grammar_de: A 没有 B + Adjektiv bedeutet „A ist nicht so … wie B“: 我做的饺子没有奶奶的布丁好看 „meine Jiaozi sehen nicht so schön aus wie Omas Puddings“. Vergleiche A 比 B 还 + Adjektiv, „A ist noch …er als B“: 比她想的还好吃 „noch leckerer, als sie gedacht hatte“.
items.grammar_pt: A 没有 B + adjetivo significa “A não é tão … quanto B”: 我做的饺子没有奶奶的布丁好看 “os meus jiaozi não são tão bonitos quanto os puddings da vovó”. Compare com A 比 B 还 + adjetivo, “A é ainda mais … que B”: 比她想的还好吃 “ainda mais gostoso do que ela tinha imaginado”.
questions: 小月为什么以为饭后有甜的东西？
约克郡布丁是用什么做的？要怎么吃？
